title: The One Ring
kind: Ruling Ring of Sauron
blurb: The master ring that Sauron forged in Mount Doom to rule all other Rings of Power, and that was unmade there in T.A. 3019.
book:
Sauron forged the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom about S.A. 1600. He poured much of his own strength into it. It ruled the other Rings of Power and gave long life without peace to its bearer.

At the end of the Second Age, Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand. He kept it instead of destroying it. In T.A. 2 Orcs ambushed him near the Gladden Fields. The Ring slipped from his finger in the Anduin, and the Orcs slew him.

The Ring lay in the Anduin until Déagol found it there in about T.A. 2463. Sméagol killed him for it and became Gollum. He hid under the Misty Mountains for centuries. Bilbo found it there in T.A. 2941.

Frodo inherited the Ring and bore it from Bag End to Mordor. Gollum seized it at the Cracks of Doom and fell into the fire with it. The Ring was destroyed on 25 March, T.A. 3019, and Sauron's power ended.
film: The films show Isildur refusing to cast the Ring into the fire when Elrond urges him. The prologue shows Sauron as a giant armoured figure on the slopes of Mount Doom.

facts.Owners: Sauron, Isildur, Déagol, Gollum, Bilbo, Frodo, Samwise (briefly)
facts.Fate: Destroyed in the Cracks of Doom, T.A. 3019

places.note: Sauron forges the Ring in the fires of Orodruin about S.A. 1600.
Isildur cuts the Ring from Sauron at the end of the siege of Barad-dûr.
Orcs ambush Isildur, and the Ring slips from him into the Anduin in T.A. 2.
Déagol finds the Ring in the Anduin by the Gladden Fields about T.A. 2463.
Gollum keeps the Ring by his lake under the mountains; Bilbo finds it there in T.A. 2941.
Bilbo and then Frodo keep the Ring at Bag End.
Gollum falls with the Ring into the fire, and it is unmade on 25 March, T.A. 3019.

title: Narya
kind: Elven Ring of Power, the Ring of Fire
blurb: The red-stoned Elven ring of fire, one of the Three, kept by Círdan and later borne by Gandalf.
book:
Narya was one of the Three Rings made by Celebrimbor of Eregion. Sauron did not touch the Three, and they were made without his help. Celebrimbor hid them from him when the One Ring was forged.

By one account, Celebrimbor gave Narya and Vilya to Gil-galad of Lindon, and Gil-galad gave Narya to Círdan. Círdan kept it at the Grey Havens for a long age.

When Gandalf arrived at the Grey Havens, Círdan gave him the Ring. He knew that Gandalf would need it for his work. Gandalf bore it in secret through the Third Age. It helped him kindle courage in others against despair.

When the One Ring was destroyed, the power of the Three ended. Gandalf took Narya over the Sea in T.A. 3021.

facts.Fate: Borne over the Sea by Gandalf, T.A. 3021

title: Nenya
kind: Elven Ring of Power, the Ring of Adamant
blurb: The white-stoned Elven ring of adamant, one of the Three, borne by Galadriel and used to guard Lothlórien.
book:
Nenya was one of the Three Rings of the Elves. Celebrimbor made it in Eregion, and it was set with a white stone. It was hidden from Sauron and did not serve him.

Celebrimbor gave Nenya to Galadriel. She wore it for the rest of the Third Age. The Ring slowed the passing of time and shielded the Elven realm that she and Celeborn ruled.

Under the power of Nenya, Lothlórien stayed fair and hard to enter. Its strength helped to turn back the assaults that came from Dol Guldur.

Galadriel knew that the Ring would fail if the One was destroyed. She accepted this and still helped the Quest. In T.A. 3021 she passed over the Sea from the Grey Havens, and Nenya went with her.

facts.Fate: Borne over the Sea by Galadriel in T.A. 3021

title: Vilya
kind: Elven Ring of Power, the Ring of Air
blurb: The mightiest of the Three Elven rings, set with a blue stone and borne by Gil-galad and then Elrond.
book:
Vilya was the greatest of the Three Rings. Celebrimbor made it in Eregion, and it was set with a blue gem. It was hidden from Sauron and never touched by his hand.

Celebrimbor gave Vilya and Narya to Gil-galad, the High King of the Noldor in Lindon. Gil-galad gave Vilya to Elrond, his herald, and Elrond bore it from then on.

Elrond used Vilya to protect Rivendell and to preserve its peace and beauty. The Ring healed and sustained rather than conquered.

Its power ended when the One Ring was unmade. Elrond left Middle-earth from the Grey Havens in T.A. 3021 and took Vilya over the Sea.

facts.Fate: Borne over the Sea by Elrond in T.A. 3021

title: Seven Rings
kind: Rings of Power given to the Dwarf-lords
blurb: The Rings that Sauron gave to the Dwarf-lords; dragons consumed four, and Sauron took back the other three.
book:
The Seven Rings were made in the Second Age, in the time when Sauron worked with the Elven-smiths of Eregion. Sauron gave them to the lords of the Dwarves. The Dwarves of Durin's line said that their own Ring came to Durin III from the Elven-smiths, not from Sauron.

The Dwarves did not become slaves of Sauron, as the Men of the Nine did. The Rings did not bend their wills. They did stir in their owners a deep hunger for gold.

The Rings also made the Dwarves' hoards grow. This drew dragons to their halls. Dragons consumed four of the Seven, and Sauron took back the other three.

The last to be found was the Ring of Durin's line, held by Thrór and then by Thráin II. Sauron took it from Thráin in Dol Guldur in T.A. 2845. After the One was destroyed, the power of all the Rings ended.

facts.Made by: Sauron with the Elven-smiths of Eregion
facts.Fate: Four consumed by dragons; three retaken by Sauron

places.note: The Seven are made in Eregion during the years of the Elven-smiths.
The Ring of Durin's line is kept in Khazad-dûm until the Dwarves flee the Balrog in T.A. 1981.

title: Nine Rings
kind: Rings of Power given to Men
blurb: The Rings of Power given to nine mortal kings, whose bearers faded into the Nazgûl, servants of Sauron.
book:
The Nine Rings were made in the Second Age, in the time when Sauron worked among the Elven-smiths of Eregion. Sauron gave them to mortal Men, mostly great lords and kings.

The Rings gave their bearers long life and power. They also bound the bearers to the will of the One Ring. Little by little the nine Men faded and became wraiths.

These nine were the Ringwraiths, or Nazgûl. They served Sauron through the Second and Third Ages. Their chief was the Witch-king of Angmar.

Sauron kept the Nine himself after their bearers became wraiths. When the One Ring was unmade, the Nazgûl lost their power and their forms and perished.

facts.Made by: Sauron with the Elven-smiths of Eregion
facts.Owners: Nine mortal kings, then the Nazgûl
facts.Fate: Their power ended with the unmaking of the One Ring

places.note: The Nine are made in Eregion in the days of the Elven-smiths.

title: Ring of Thrór
kind: Dwarf Ring of Power, last of the Seven
blurb: The last of the Seven Rings held by the line of Durin, taken from Thráin II by Sauron in T.A. 2845.
book:
This was the last of the Seven Rings that the kings of the Dwarves of Durin's line held. The Dwarves said it was given to Durin III by the Elven-smiths. It passed down from father to son and made their hoard of gold grow.

Thrór owned it when Smaug took the Lonely Mountain in T.A. 2770. Thrór fled with his people and wandered in exile. He was murdered by the orc Azog at the gate of Moria in T.A. 2790.

Before he went to Moria, Thrór gave the Ring to his son Thráin II. Thráin later set out for Erebor, carrying the Ring. Sauron's servants caught him and held him in the dungeons of Dol Guldur.

Sauron took the Ring from Thráin in T.A. 2845. Thráin died there. Gandalf found him and received Thrór's map and key, but the Ring was not recovered.

facts.Owners: Kings of Durin's line, including Thrór and Thráin II

title: Arkenstone
kind: Great white jewel, Heart of the Mountain
blurb: The great white gem of Erebor, the heirloom of Thrór's house, taken by Bilbo and buried with Thorin.
book:
The Arkenstone was a great white jewel that shone with a light of its own. The Dwarves found it deep under Erebor in the days of Thráin I. They called it the Heart of the Mountain.

Thrór and his heirs prized it above all their treasure. When Smaug took the Mountain, the Arkenstone lay in his hoard.

Bilbo found it in the dragon's lair in T.A. 2941 and hid it from Thorin. Thorin longed for it above all the rest of the hoard. Bilbo gave it in secret to Bard and the Elvenking, hoping to buy peace.

Thorin was furious and sent Bilbo away. Thorin was mortally wounded in the Battle of Five Armies and made peace with Bilbo before he died. Bard laid the Arkenstone on his breast, and he was buried with it deep in the Mountain.
film: In the Hobbit films the Arkenstone is the focus of Thorin's gold-sickness. Bilbo hides it and offers it to Bard and Thranduil in the camp before the battle.

facts.Owners: Kings of Durin's line from Thráin I to Thrór, then Smaug's hoard, Bilbo, Bard
facts.Fate: Buried with Thorin beneath the Lonely Mountain

places.note: The Dwarves find the gem deep under the Lonely Mountain.
The Arkenstone lies in the hoard of the Kingdom under the Mountain.

title: Elessar (the Elfstone)
kind: Green gem of healing in an eagle brooch
blurb: A green gem in a silver eagle brooch, given by Galadriel to Aragorn, who took its name as his own.
book:
The Elessar was a clear green gem set in a silver brooch shaped like an eagle with spread wings. Light through it was said to heal and renew living things.

In The Lord of the Rings, Galadriel says that she gave the stone to her daughter Celebrían, and Celebrían gave it to Arwen. Unfinished Tales gives two older tales of its making. In one, Enerdhil of Gondolin made it. In the other, Celebrimbor made it for Galadriel.

Galadriel gave the Elfstone to Aragorn in Lothlórien in T.A. 3019, as the Fellowship left. It was a token of hope, and she told him to take the name that had been foretold for him.

Aragorn wore it in the War of the Ring. After the victory he took Elessar as his royal name, and his house was called the House of Elessar.
film: In the films Arwen gives Aragorn a jewel on a chain in Rivendell. That pendant is a different object from the brooch of the book.

facts.Kind: Green gem in an eagle-shaped brooch
facts.Made by: Enerdhil of Gondolin, or Celebrimbor, by two accounts in Unfinished Tales
facts.Fate: Kept by Aragorn and his line

places.note: Galadriel gives the Elfstone to Aragorn when the Fellowship leaves Lothlórien.
Aragorn takes the name Elessar as King of Gondor.

title: Star of Elendil
kind: White gem worn on the brow of kings
blurb: A white gem bound on the brow of Elendil and the Kings of Arnor, later worn by Aragorn.
book:
The Elendilmir was a white gem bound on a fillet and worn on the brow. It shone like a star. Elendil wore it as King of Arnor, and it became the token of the northern kings.

Isildur wore the first Elendilmir when Orcs slew him at the Gladden Fields in T.A. 2, and it was lost there. His son Valandil had a second gem made in Rivendell. The Kings of Arnor and Arthedain wore it, and Elrond later kept it with the other heirlooms of Isildur's line.

In the War of the Ring, Aragorn bore the Star of Elendil upon his brow. After the war the first Elendilmir was found in Orthanc, where Saruman had hidden it. Aragorn wore it on high days as King.

facts.Fate: The first gem was found in Orthanc and worn by Aragorn as King

places.note: The Kings of Arnor wear the Elendilmir in their city of Annúminas.
The first Elendilmir is lost with Isildur at the Gladden Fields in T.A. 2.
A second gem is made in Rivendell for Valandil and later kept there.
Aragorn wears the Star of Elendil in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.
The first Elendilmir is found in Orthanc after the fall of Saruman.

title: Necklace of Girion
kind: Emerald necklace of the Lord of Dale
blurb: A necklace of five hundred emeralds that Girion of Dale paid to the Dwarves for armour for his son.
book:
Girion was the Lord of Dale in the days before Smaug came. He owned a necklace of five hundred emeralds, green as grass.

He gave it to the Dwarves of Erebor as payment for a coat of mail for his eldest son. The coat was made of silver rings and was as strong as triple steel. The necklace lay in the hoard of the Mountain when Smaug took it.

Smaug destroyed Dale, but Girion's wife and child escaped. Bard of Lake-town came from their line. After the Battle of Five Armies, Dáin gave the emeralds to Bard. Bard then gave them to the Elvenking, who loved such jewels.

facts.Fate: Given by Bard to the Elvenking

The Dwarves hold the necklace in Erebor before the dragon comes.

title: Phial of Galadriel
kind: Crystal phial holding starlight
blurb: A small crystal phial holding the light of Eärendil's star, given by Galadriel to Frodo in Lothlórien.
book:
The Phial of Galadriel was a small crystal vessel that held the light of Eärendil's star. Galadriel had caught that light in the water of her fountain.

She gave it to Frodo in Lothlórien in T.A. 3019. She said it would be a light to him in dark places when other lights failed.

Frodo held it up in Shelob's lair, and its light drove her back. Sam later used it against Shelob when she attacked Frodo. Sam also used it to pass the Two Watchers at the gate of the Tower of Cirith Ungol.

In the Sammath Naur the power of the Phial grew faint. Sam gave it back to Frodo, and the books do not tell its later fate.
film: In the films Frodo raises the Phial in Shelob's lair, and Sam later uses it when he fights her.

facts.Fate: Not stated after the Quest

places.note: Galadriel gives the Phial to Frodo before the Fellowship departs.
Frodo lifts the Phial against Shelob in her lair.
Sam uses the Phial to break the will of the Two Watchers at the tower gate.

title: Andúril
kind: Sword of the kings of Gondor, reforged Narsil
blurb: The sword Narsil of Elendil, reforged in Rivendell and borne by Aragorn as Andúril, Flame of the West.
book:
Narsil was the sword of Elendil. Telchar of Nogrod made it in the First Age. Elendil carried it in the Last Alliance, and it broke beneath him when Sauron slew him.

Isildur used a shard of it to cut the One Ring from Sauron's hand. The broken pieces were kept by Isildur's heirs for ages. They stayed in Rivendell with Elrond.

Before the Fellowship left Rivendell in T.A. 3018, Elven smiths forged the sword anew. Aragorn named it Andúril.

Aragorn bore it at Helm's Deep, in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields and at the Black Gate. Its fate after he became king is not stated.
film: In the films Elrond brings the reforged sword to Aragorn at Dunharrow and urges him to take the Paths of the Dead.

facts.Fate: Borne by Aragorn as King Elessar

Narsil breaks beneath Elendil and Isildur cuts the Ring from Sauron with a shard.
The shards are kept in Rivendell and reforged as Andúril in T.A. 3018.
Aragorn bears Andúril in the defence of Helm's Deep.
Aragorn leads the assault at the Pelennor Fields with Andúril.
Aragorn bears Andúril in the last battle before the Black Gate.

title: Sting
kind: Elvish short sword of the Hobbits
blurb: An Elvish blade from the trolls' hoard that Bilbo named Sting; it glowed blue when Orcs were near.
book:
Sting was an Elvish knife made long before. Bilbo found it in the stone-trolls' lair in T.A. 2941. It was only a knife to the trolls, but a short sword to a Hobbit.

Bilbo named it Sting in Mirkwood, after he used it to kill spiders. The blade glowed with a blue light when Orcs were near.

Bilbo gave Sting to Frodo in Rivendell before the Fellowship set out. Frodo used it in Moria, in the Chamber of Mazarbul. Sam later took Sting when he thought Frodo was dead.

Sam used Sting to wound and drive off Shelob. Its fate after the end of the Third Age is not stated.
film: In the films Bilbo gives Sting to Frodo in Rivendell. Frodo and Sam both use it against Shelob.

facts.Fate: Not stated after T.A. 3019

title: Glamdring
kind: Elven sword of Gondolin, borne by Gandalf
blurb: The Elven sword from the trolls' hoard that Gandalf bore as Glamdring, called Beater by the Orcs.
book:
Glamdring was an Elven sword made in Gondolin in the First Age. It was one of three blades that Thorin's company and Gandalf found in the trolls' cave in T.A. 2941.

Gandalf took it, and Thorin took Orcrist. Elrond told them that the blades came from Gondolin. Glamdring had once belonged to the King of Gondolin. The Orcs called Glamdring Beater, because they hated and feared it.

Gandalf slew the Great Goblin with it. He bore Glamdring through the War of the Ring. He drew it in the Mines of Moria when the Balrog came, and fought on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm.

After he returned as the White, he kept Glamdring.

facts.Owners: The King of Gondolin (Turgon), then Gandalf
facts.Fate: Not stated

places.note: The Elves of Gondolin make Glamdring in the First Age.
Gandalf finds the sword in the stone-trolls' cave in T.A. 2941.
Gandalf slays the Great Goblin with Glamdring in Goblin-town.
Gandalf draws Glamdring against the Balrog on the Bridge of Khazad-dûm.

The Lord of the Rings, Book II, Chapter 5

title: Orcrist
kind: Elven sword of Gondolin, borne by Thorin
blurb: The Elven sword from the trolls' hoard that Thorin bore, called Goblin-cleaver and laid on his tomb.
book:
Orcrist was an Elven sword made in Gondolin in the First Age. It was found with Glamdring in the trolls' cave in T.A. 2941. The Goblins called it Biter and hated it.

Thorin Oakenshield took Orcrist as his weapon and used it in the goblin tunnels. The Elves of Mirkwood took it from him when they captured the Dwarves, and the Elvenking kept it.

Thorin fell in the Battle of Five Armies. The Elvenking then laid Orcrist on Thorin's tomb under the Mountain. It was said to gleam in the dark when foes drew near, so the Dwarves could not be taken by surprise.

facts.Fate: Laid on Thorin's tomb under the Lonely Mountain

Thorin's company find the sword in the stone-trolls' cave.
The Elvenking takes Orcrist from Thorin and keeps it in his halls.
The Elvenking lays Orcrist on Thorin's tomb under the Mountain.

title: Mithril coat
kind: Shirt of mithril rings
blurb: A shirt of mithril rings that Thorin gave to Bilbo; Frodo wore it on the quest to Mordor.
book:
This was a small shirt of mithril rings. It had been made long before for some Elf-prince, and it shone like silver. Thorin gave it to Bilbo from the hoard of Erebor in T.A. 2941.

Gandalf thought it was worth more than the whole Shire. Bilbo lent it for a time to the Mathom-house at Michel Delving. In Rivendell he gave it to Frodo, who wore it under his clothes.

The coat saved Frodo's life in Moria when an Orc-chief speared him in the Chamber of Mazarbul.

Orcs stripped it from Frodo in the Tower of Cirith Ungol. The Mouth of Sauron showed it at the Black Gate as a false token, and Gandalf took it. Frodo had it again later, and it turned Saruman's knife in the Shire.
film: In the films the mithril coat saves Frodo from a cave troll in Moria.

facts.Fate: Kept by Frodo after the Quest

title: Black Arrow
kind: Heirloom arrow of the house of Girion
blurb: The last black arrow of Girion's house, fired by Bard to slay Smaug in T.A. 2941.
book:
The Black Arrow was an heirloom of Bard's house, the line of Girion, Lord of Dale. Bard had it from his father, and his father from older days. Bard believed it came from the forges of the King under the Mountain.

It was the last arrow in his quiver. Bard held it when Smaug attacked Lake-town in T.A. 2941. A thrush told him of a bare place on the dragon's chest.

Bard fitted the arrow to his bow. He shot it into the weak place, and the arrow sank deep. Smaug died and fell on Lake-town.

The books do not say what became of the arrow.
film: In the Hobbit films Bard fires the black arrow from a tower with his son Bain as a support.

facts.Fate: Not stated after the shot

places.note: Bard fires the arrow from Lake-town and slays Smaug.
The arrow is an heirloom of the line of Girion of Dale.

title: Barrow-blades
kind: Daggers of Westernesse
blurb: Daggers of the Men of Westernesse taken from the Barrow-downs; Merry's blade helped to destroy the Witch-king.
book:
The Barrow-blades were long daggers made by the Men of Westernesse in the North Kingdom. They were forged long ago for the war against the evil realm of Angmar. They carried spells against its lord.

A Barrow-wight caught the four hobbits on the Barrow-downs. Tom Bombadil freed them and brought out the treasure of the barrow. He chose a blade for each hobbit.

Frodo struck at the Witch-king with his blade on Weathertop. It broke at the Ford of Bruinen when he raised it against the Riders. Merry stabbed the Witch-king with his blade on the Pelennor Fields. The blade helped Éowyn slay him, but it withered away.

Pippin used his blade to kill a troll at the Black Gate.

facts.Fate: Frodo's blade broke at the Ford of Bruinen; Merry's withered away at the Pelennor Fields

places.note: Tom Bombadil takes the blades from the barrow and gives one to each hobbit.
Frodo strikes at the Witch-king with his blade on Weathertop.
Frodo's blade breaks when he raises it against the Riders at the ford.
Merry stabs the Witch-king, and his blade withers away.
Pippin slays a troll with his blade at the Black Gate.

title: Morgul-knife
kind: Enchanted knife of the Witch-king
blurb: The Witch-king's evil knife that wounded Frodo on Weathertop; its blade melted away and a splinter stayed in the wound.
book:
The Morgul-knife was a long, cruel knife of the Witch-king of Angmar. It was a weapon of the Nazgûl and worked with a dark spell.

On Weathertop in T.A. 3018, the Witch-king stabbed Frodo with it. The blade melted away. A splinter stayed inside the wound and worked its way toward the heart.

This sort of wound turned a victim into a wraith. Frodo was in great danger. Aragorn eased the pain with athelas.

Elrond drew out the splinter in Rivendell, and Frodo recovered. The wound still troubled Frodo on its anniversary for the rest of his days in Middle-earth.
film: In the films Arwen carries the wounded Frodo to the Ford. In the book Glorfindel finds him, and Frodo rides alone across the Ford.

facts.Fate: Blade melted away on Weathertop

places.note: The Witch-king wounds Frodo with the knife on Weathertop.
The Nazgûl attack the hobbits and Aragorn in this fight.
Elrond removes the splinter and heals Frodo in Rivendell.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book I, Chapters 11 and 12

title: Grond
kind: Battering-ram of Mordor
blurb: The great battering-ram of Mordor, named after Morgoth's hammer, that broke the Gate of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019.
book:
Grond was a great battering-ram carried by Sauron's armies to Minas Tirith. It was named after the mace of Morgoth, which was called the Hammer of the Underworld.

The ram was forged in the dark smithies of Mordor. It was shaped like a wolf's head and bound with spells of ruin. Many beasts dragged it forward on the road.

The Witch-king urged his troops to use it on the Great Gate of Minas Tirith. After three blows, the gates were broken.

It was in use only in the siege and in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. The books do not say what became of it.
film: The films show the ram Grond with a wolf's-head and Orcs hauling it up to the Gate.

facts.Fate: Not stated

places.note: The ram is forged in the dark smithies of Mordor.
Grond breaks the Great Gate of Minas Tirith on the third stroke.
The assault comes in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

sources: The Lord of the Rings, Book V, Chapter 4
